grid.projection: Web Mercator pixel grid (cell centres at x0+j+0.5, y0+i+0.5 global pixels)

dem_water.note: Flat water surface recorded in the elevation data (SRTM, February 2000). Vertical datum EGM96; published levels use the national (Baltic) height system, so offsets of the order of a metre are possible.

bits.1: inside the lake outline of OpenStreetMap
bits.2: dam body: cannot be flooded or crossed

dam.name: Kayrakkum Dam
dam.note: Cells of the dam body (OpenStreetMap outline, widened by 1.5 cells, above the water) cannot be flooded or crossed.

elevation.name: Terrain Tiles (Mapzen/Tilezen) on AWS Open Data, zoom 10; SRTM (NASA/USGS) in this region
elevation.licence: SRTM: public domain; attribution per Tilezen

outline.name: OpenStreetMap (lake and dam outlines, place names)
outline.note: The outline shows the shore when it was mapped (date not recorded). It is drawn for orientation and not used in calculations.

precipitation.name: NASA POWER climatology, PRECTOTCORR (MERRA-2 based)
precipitation.period: 25-year Meteorological and Solar Monthly & Annual Climatologies (January 2001 - December 2025)
precipitation.note: One 0.5° × 0.625° grid cell over the lake; rain on the lake only, not the catchment.

published.citation: Qairokkum HPP Climate Resilience Upgrade. Environmental and Social Appraisal and Action Plan (project 47253), Table 1.

full_supply_level_masl.where: Table 1, PDF p. 4 (the same level in CAWater-Info and the 2000 dam safety report)

storage_table.where: Table 1, PDF p. 4–5: active storage volume 2300 million m³ “acc. to 2009 survey” between the minimum operation level and the full supply level
storage_table.note: Approximate. No level–volume curve was found for this reservoir, so the change is taken as a straight line between two published levels (333 million m³ per metre). The real lake is wider near the top: this line gives too little near the full level and too much near the lowest level. A change, not the volume stored today.

mean_inflow_m3s.where: Kayrakkum Dam Safety Assessment Report (2000), p. 12: long-term average discharge of the river at the dam site

facts.label: Water surface at the full level
facts.where: CAWater-Info reservoir card; dam safety report (2000)

facts.label: Total volume at the full level, as designed
Total volume at the full level, 2009 survey
Lost to sediment since construction
facts.where: GCF FP040, p. 50; about 10 million m³ per year today

notes: Published volumes disagree because they refer to different years and lower levels: 4.0–4.2 km³ as designed, 3.0 km³ in the 2009 survey. They are shown side by side and never mixed in a calculation.
The lowest level is 340.6 m in the 2009-based appraisal and 342.5 m (“dead storage level”) in the 2000 dam safety report. The appraisal's value is used, together with its own storage figure.
No published evaporation figure for this reservoir was found. Evaporation is therefore an input you set yourself (0 by default), not data.
None of the documents states which height system its levels use.
